source_digest_method: sorted Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/**/*.rs and examples/**/*.rs; relative path + NUL + bytes + NUL per file
binary_provenance: Each run records its executable digest. The final executable is rebuilt from the recorded current source. Earlier per-run executable hashes identify the same retained algorithms before audit wrapper/test-only edits. Hand/torus accepted runs used the retained coarse-scalar/fine-table algorithms. The separately recorded fine-scalar experiment was reverted.

upstream.solver: MapleCOMSPS_LRB simp executable built from pinned tree

research.notes: Scalar coordinate encoding, growing mutable regions and residual inversions near orientation singularities. This motivates inspecting the field at the junction; it does not establish a singularity-placement cause for this fixture.

retained: Scalar-coordinate SAT for coarse repair, using the existing Rust Batsat engine.
Fixed axes and correlated edge domains retained; decoded assignments independently checked for domain membership, closure and nonnegative area.
Audit export/replay of frozen local problems and exact upstream DIMACS engine comparison.
unchanged: Coarse patch selection and hierarchy traversal
changes.rejected: Applying the scalar encoding to fine repair completed with 80 inversions, whereas the retained table fallback completed with 64. That change was reverted.

comparison.timing_note: Single controlled runs. Wall times, search-only times and parse/encoding-inclusive times are labeled separately; no general benchmark claim.

boundary_controls.wide_control_caution: Radius 8 merges the 64- and 21-inversion regions and times out. At radius 16 the junction exceeds the export guard; the exported 14-fold patch is not the junction. Its UNSAT outcome is excluded from junction conclusions.

free_boundary_assignment.note: Independent integer geometry verification of the upstream free-boundary model. Not applicable to the full mesh: changed cut-edge values would need a compatible solve outside the patch.

boundary_controls.interpretation: The frozen fixed-boundary patch is infeasible. Removing fixed boundary values allows a geometrically verified integer assignment that changes 17 fixed edges. It is not a valid whole-mesh replacement and does not establish whole-model or orientation-field infeasibility.

limits: Coarse target hand remains rejected in the exact retained implementation (264 quads, nine bad diagonals); the fine-scalar trial also did not fix it.
SAT infeasibility is local with fixed frames, boundaries and domains, not a proof against the global retopology problem.
Native scalar clause order/search/budgets differ from pinned upstream; semantic equivalence is tested, solver decisions need not match.
Retained fine fallback still has expensive searches; completed-pass checkpoints do not preserve partial fine-stage progress.
No self-intersection certificate, app integration, adaptive paint, multi-path UI or platform validation.
